plain_description.what: Draws the full accuracy curve for routing the least certain questions to the best single model instead of the per-cell choice, at every coverage level. It compares this with sending a random set of questions of the same size. Uses about 5,900 evaluation questions. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: Checks whether the routing's uncertainty signal is a useful safety valve: does escalating uncertain items first beat escalating at random?
plain_description.information: A positive area means the uncertainty ordering helps. A negative area would remove it as a safety valve. Result: averaged over the coverage levels tested, escalating uncertain items first beats escalating at random by about +0.66 accuracy points, which is small. It is not a gain at every level: at high coverage the interval at each level includes zero. A plain k-means partition does the same (+0.60), so this is not a property of the tree. There is no usable operating point: the chosen coverage's gain includes zero, and escalating at very low coverage lowers accuracy.
